name: article
description: Fetch a Twitter Article (long-form content) and export as Markdown

args.name: tweet-id
args.help: Tweet ID or URL containing the article

name: bookmark-folder
description: Read the tweets inside a single Twitter/X bookmark folder. Get the folder id from `opencli twitter bookmark-folders`.

args.name: folder-id
args.help: Folder id from `opencli twitter bookmark-folders`.

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of bookmarks to return (default 20).

args.name: top-by-engagement
args.help: When set to N>0, re-rank the folder by weighted engagement (likes×1 + retweets×3 + replies×2 + bookmarks×5 + log10(views+1)×0.5) and return the top N. Default 0 keeps the API's native (saved-time) ordering.

name: bookmark-folders
description: List your Twitter/X bookmark folders (the user-created collections under Bookmarks). Returns folder id, name, item count, and created_at.

name: bookmarks
description: Fetch your Twitter/X bookmarks (the logged-in user's saved tweets, newest first)

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of bookmarks to return (default 20). Ignored when --all is set.

args.name: all
args.help: Fetch all bookmark pages until exhausted. Prefer --output-file for large archives.

args.name: resume-file
args.help: Resume file for long-running all-pages bookmark syncs.

args.name: output-file
args.help: Write all-page results to JSONL. Requires --all and --resume-file.

args.name: max-pages
args.help: Optional pagination safety cap (default 100; raised automatically with --all).

args.name: top-by-engagement
args.help: When set to N>0, re-rank the bookmarks by weighted engagement (likes×1 + retweets×3 + replies×2 + bookmarks×5 + log10(views+1)×0.5) and return the top N. Default 0 keeps the API's native (saved-time) ordering. Incompatible with --output-file.

name: collection
description: Fetch a user timeline with relationship facts and a bounded completion receipt.

args.name: username
args.help: Twitter screen name (with or without @).

args.name: until
args.help: RFC3339 lower time boundary that must be reached or exhausted.

args.name: limit
args.help: Safety ceiling; reaching it is a typed failure.

args.name: page-delay
args.help: Seconds to wait between cursor pages.

name: device-follow
description: Read the /i/timeline device-follow notification stream (tweets aggregated under a bell-icon "new posts from @userA and N others" notification)

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of tweets to return (1-200, default 20)

args.name: top-by-engagement
args.help: When set to N>0, re-rank by weighted engagement and return the top N. Default 0 keeps upstream ordering.

name: download
description: Download Twitter/X media (images and videos). Provide either <username> to fetch every media item from their profile via the GraphQL UserMedia endpoint with cursor pagination, or --tweet-url to download a single tweet.

args.name: username
args.help: Twitter username (with or without @) to scan their profile media. Either <username> or --tweet-url is required.

args.name: tweet-url
args.help: Single tweet URL to download. Use this OR <username>, not both required at once.

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of media items to download when scanning a profile (default 10). Ignored when --tweet-url is used.

args.name: output
args.help: Output directory (default ./twitter-downloads). A per-source subdir is created inside.

name: followers
description: Get accounts following a Twitter/X user (defaults to the logged-in user when no user is given)

args.name: user
args.help: Twitter/X handle (with or without @). Omit to fetch followers of the currently logged-in account.

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of follower rows to return (default 50). Must be a positive integer.

name: following
description: Get accounts a Twitter/X user is following (defaults to the logged-in user when no user is given)

args.name: user
args.help: Twitter/X handle (with or without @). Omit to fetch the accounts the currently logged-in user follows.

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of following rows to return (default 50). Must be a positive integer.

name: likes
description: Fetch liked tweets of a Twitter user (defaults to the logged-in user when no username is given)

args.name: username
args.help: Twitter screen name (with or without @). Defaults to the logged-in user when omitted.

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of liked tweets to return (default 20). Ignored when --all is set.

args.name: all
args.help: Fetch all liked-tweet pages until exhausted. Prefer --output-file for large archives.

args.name: resume-file
args.help: Resume file for long-running all-pages likes syncs.

args.name: output-file
args.help: Write all-page results to JSONL. Requires --all and --resume-file.

args.name: max-pages
args.help: Optional pagination safety cap (default 100; raised automatically with --all).

args.name: top-by-engagement
args.help: When set to N>0, re-rank the liked tweets by weighted engagement (likes×1 + retweets×3 + replies×2 + bookmarks×5 + log10(views+1)×0.5) and return the top N. Default 0 keeps the API's native (recency) ordering. Incompatible with --output-file.

name: list-tweets
description: Fetch tweets from a Twitter/X list timeline

args.name: listId
args.help: Numeric ID of a Twitter/X list (e.g. from `opencli twitter lists`)

args.name: top-by-engagement
args.help: When set to N>0, re-rank the list timeline by weighted engagement (likes×1 + retweets×3 + replies×2 + bookmarks×5 + log10(views+1)×0.5) and return the top N. Default 0 keeps the list's native (recency) ordering.

name: lists
description: Get Twitter/X lists for the logged-in user (owned + subscribed)

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of lists to return (default 50).

name: notifications
description: Get your Twitter/X notifications (the logged-in user's likes/replies/follows feed, newest first)

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of notifications to return (default 20).

name: profile
description: Fetch a Twitter user profile — bio, stats, etc. (defaults to the logged-in user when no username is given)

args.name: username
args.help: Twitter screen name (with or without @). Defaults to the logged-in user when omitted.

name: search
description: Search Twitter/X for tweets, with optional --from / --has / --exclude / --product filters mapped to X's search operators

args.name: query
args.help: Search query. Raw X operators (e.g. "exact phrase", #tag, OR, lang:en, since:YYYY-MM-DD, from:, since:) are passed through unchanged.

args.name: filter
args.help: Legacy alias for --product. Kept for backwards compatibility; if --product is set it wins.

args.name: product
args.help: Which X search tab to read: top (default), live (Latest), photos, videos. Maps to the f= URL param.

args.name: from
args.help: Restrict to tweets authored by <user>. Leading @ is stripped. Equivalent to appending `from:<user>` to the query.

args.name: has
args.help: Restrict to tweets that have media|images|videos|links|replies. Maps to X's `filter:<has>` operator.

args.name: exclude
args.help: Exclude tweets matching <type>: replies|retweets|media|links. Maps to X's `-filter:<x>` operator (retweets → -filter:nativeretweets).

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of tweets to return (default 15). Result count after server-side filtering.

args.name: top-by-engagement
args.help: When set to N>0, re-rank the results by weighted engagement (likes×1 + retweets×3 + replies×2 + bookmarks×5 + log10(views+1)×0.5) and return the top N. Default 0 keeps X's native ordering.

name: thread
description: Get a tweet thread (original + all replies)

args.name: tweet-id
args.help: Tweet numeric ID (e.g. 1234567890) or full status URL

args.name: top-by-engagement
args.help: When set to N>0, re-rank the thread by weighted engagement (likes×1 + retweets×3 + replies×2 + bookmarks×5 + log10(views+1)×0.5) and return the top N. Default 0 keeps the conversation's structural ordering.

name: timeline
description: Fetch the logged-in user's home timeline (for-you algorithmic feed by default; pass --type following for the chronological feed of accounts you follow)

args.name: type
args.help: Which home-timeline feed to read. Default for-you (algorithmic). Use following for the chronological feed of accounts you follow.

args.name: limit
args.help: Maximum number of tweets to return (default 20).

args.name: top-by-engagement
args.help: When set to N>0, re-rank the timeline by weighted engagement (likes×1 + retweets×3 + replies×2 + bookmarks×5 + log10(views+1)×0.5) and return the top N. Default 0 keeps X's native ordering.

name: trending
description: Twitter/X trending topics

args.name: limit
args.help: Number of trends to show

name: tweets
description: Fetch a Twitter user's most recent tweets (chronological, excludes pinned; defaults to the logged-in user when no username is given)

args.name: username
args.help: Twitter screen name (with or without @). Defaults to the logged-in user when omitted.

args.name: limit
args.help: Max tweets to return (1-10000; fetched across cursor pages)

args.name: page-delay
args.help: Seconds to wait between paginated timeline requests to reduce rate-limit risk. Use 0 to disable.

args.name: top-by-engagement
args.help: When set to N>0, re-rank the tweets by weighted engagement (likes×1 + retweets×3 + replies×2 + bookmarks×5 + log10(views+1)×0.5) and return the top N. Default 0 keeps the chronological ordering.

name: whoami
description: Show the current logged-in twitter account
